subject: A question of running codex on new samples without re-normalize all pooled samples

messages.author: ca0919c19fb81f56
messages.subject: A question of running codex on new samples without re-normalize all pooled samples
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

After trying your tool, we really like it.  But few things we want to find out if it is available.  First, We want to normalize the pooled samples once and when there is a new sample, we just want to call CNVs on the new sample based on the normalization on the pooled samples, instead of running the whole process all over again.  Is it doable?  For example, if we have few hundreds or even thousands of samples that we can pool together for normalization, but we only want to call CNVs on some new samples that are not in the pool.

It might be even better if you have a p-value or FDR to indicate the likelihood of having a CNV at the location is not by chance.  But its a plus, not a necessary improvement.

Thank you,
Kajia

messages.author: ca0919c19fb81f56
messages.subject: Re: A question of running codex on new samples without re-normalize all pooled samples
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

This is a way on how to manage adding the new samples.  So at the read depth computing step, we can save all pooled samples as a R object, and when we have new samples, we can compute the read depth of new samples and merge the two objects together and then precede to the next step. This would save users some time and provide some flexibility.  I think u can add it in your manual page.

Thanks,
Kajia
